# didactum/lessons — contribute a lesson

> Open lessons for Didactum (https://didactum.org), a free tutor that teaches on a chalkboard and speaks aloud. One lesson is one JSON file. When a pull request is merged, the lesson plays on the site within minutes, credited to its authors.

These are the exact steps. Read them all before writing.

## 1. Where the file goes

`lessons/<subject>/<slug>.json` — lower-case letters, digits and hyphens only. The file name must equal the package `slug`. One lesson per pull request. Do not edit `schema/`, `scripts/` or other people's lessons.

Pick a topic the repo does not have yet: list `lessons/` first.

## 2. The format

Schema: `schema/lesson-package.v2.json` (published at https://didactum.org/schemas/lesson-package.v2.json). Set `"schema_version": "2.0"`.

- `id`: unique, e.g. `community.<slug>`. `slug`: same as the file name.
- `metadata`: `subject` (math, algebra, geometry, sat, physics, chemistry, reading, ...), `topic` (a human title), `concept_slugs` (1-5 kebab-case skills, most specific first), `grade_band` (k-2, 3-5, 6-8, 9-12, college, adult), optional `grade` (0-16), `language` (en), `authors` (your name or your agent's name), `license` (CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0 or CC0-1.0), `never_verbatim_verified`: true.
- `problem`: the student's problem — `statement`, `givens`, `unknown`, `assessment.answer`. The lesson never solves this problem; it teaches the method on a different worked example.
- `chapters`: each `{id, title, role?, beats}`. `role` is optional, but roles that are present must follow this order: `why` (why it matters), `history` (where it came from), `uses` (where it is used), `seek` (what the problem asks), `how` (how to solve), `check`. Titles are for humans ("Sharing one pizza"), never "Chapter 2" or a role name.
- A beat is one moment on the board:
  - `narration.text`: what the teacher says. Plain spoken words, at most 280 characters. Never `$ \ ^ = { }`: say "x squared", "equals".
  - `board.title`: at most 64 characters.
  - `board.lines`: at most 3 written lines, each at most 44 characters, at most 24 words across the beat. Equations and key terms, not sentences. `$...$` is TeX (KaTeX).
  - `board.draw`: drawing ops on a 100 x 70 board (x right 0-100, y down 0-70; keep content inside x 6-94, y 6-62). A maths or science lesson must draw something.
  - optional `checkin`: `prompt`, 2-5 `choices`, optional `branches` (what the teacher says after each choice; key = the choice text).
  - optional `prose`: reading text shown under the board.

Draw ops (all coordinates are [x, y]; `dur` is milliseconds):
- `{"op":"line","from":[x,y],"to":[x,y]}`, `{"op":"arrow","from":..,"to":..}`, `{"op":"brace","from":..,"to":..}`
- `{"op":"polyline"|"polygon"|"curve","pts":[[x,y],...]}`
- `{"op":"circle","c":[x,y],"r":5}`, `{"op":"arc","c":[x,y],"r":5,"a0":0,"a1":90}`
- `{"op":"label","at":[x,y],"text":"short","size":4.5,"align":"center"}` (a label is at most 18 characters)
- `{"op":"math","at":[x,y],"tex":"\\frac{a}{b}"}`
- `{"op":"numberline","at":[x,y],"len":70,"lo":0,"hi":10,"divisions":10,"marks":[{"v":3,"text":"A"}]}`
- `{"op":"highlight","target":"<id of an earlier op>"}`, `{"op":"pause","dur":500}`; give an op an `"id"` to target it.
- An op may carry `"say"`: one sentence spoken as it is drawn. If any op in a beat has `say`, the says together must equal `narration.text`.

## 3. A complete example

This file is valid. Copy its shape, not its topic.

```json
{
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "id": "community.same-denominator-fractions",
  "slug": "same-denominator-fractions",
  "metadata": {
    "subject": "math",
    "topic": "Adding fractions with the same bottom number",
    "concept_slugs": ["adding-fractions-like-denominators"],
    "grade_band": "3-5",
    "grade": 4,
    "language": "en",
    "authors": ["Your name or your agent's name"],
    "license": "CC-BY-4.0",
    "never_verbatim_verified": true
  },
  "problem": {
    "statement": "Ana ate 2/7 of a pizza and Ben ate 3/7 of it. What fraction of the pizza did they eat together?",
    "givens": ["Ana ate 2/7", "Ben ate 3/7"],
    "unknown": "the fraction eaten together",
    "assessment": {"answer": "5/7"}
  },
  "chapters": [
    {
      "id": "c1", "role": "why", "title": "Sharing one pizza",
      "beats": [
        {
          "id": "b1",
          "narration": {"text": "When pieces are the same size, you can just count them.", "intent": "pose"},
          "board": {
            "title": "Same-size pieces",
            "draw": [
              {"op": "circle", "c": [50, 36], "r": 22, "dur": 600},
              {"op": "line", "from": [50, 14], "to": [50, 58], "dur": 300},
              {"op": "line", "from": [28, 36], "to": [72, 36], "dur": 300}
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "c2", "role": "how", "title": "Count the slices",
      "beats": [
        {
          "id": "b2",
          "narration": {"text": "One fifth and two fifths make three fifths. The bottom number stays the same."},
          "board": {
            "title": "Add the tops",
            "lines": ["$\\frac{1}{5} + \\frac{2}{5} = \\frac{3}{5}$", "bottom stays 5"],
            "draw": [
              {"op": "polygon", "pts": [[10, 50], [90, 50], [90, 60], [10, 60]], "dur": 500},
              {"op": "line", "from": [26, 50], "to": [26, 60], "dur": 100},
              {"op": "line", "from": [42, 50], "to": [42, 60], "dur": 100},
              {"op": "line", "from": [58, 50], "to": [58, 60], "dur": 100},
              {"op": "line", "from": [74, 50], "to": [74, 60], "dur": 100},
              {"op": "label", "at": [34, 46], "text": "3 of 5", "size": 4}
            ]
          },
          "checkin": {
            "prompt": "What happens to the bottom number?",
            "choices": ["It stays the same", "We add it too"],
            "branches": {
              "It stays the same": "Yes. The slices are still fifths.",
              "We add it too": "The slices do not change size, so they are still fifths."
            }
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "b3",
          "narration": {"text": "Now add the tops of your two fractions and keep the bottom.", "intent": "celebrate"},
          "board": {
            "title": "Your turn",
            "lines": ["add the tops", "keep the bottom"],
            "draw": [{"op": "arrow", "from": [30, 40], "to": [70, 40], "dur": 400}]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## 4. Validate

```
python3 scripts/validate_lesson.py lessons/<subject>/<slug>.json
```

Python 3.9+ and nothing else. Repeat until it prints `OK`. Every error names the place (`chapters[1].beats[0] (id 'b2')`) and what to change. Without a checkout: POST the JSON to https://didactum.org/mcp/validate_lesson.

## 5. Preview

```
node scripts/preview.mjs
```

Open http://localhost:4173, pick your lesson, press "Read aloud". The preview draws each beat's board. Fix anything that sounds like a textbook.

## 6. Pull request checklist

- [ ] One new file, `lessons/<subject>/<slug>.json`, file name = slug; nothing else changed.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/validate_lesson.py` prints OK.
- [ ] The answer to `problem` appears nowhere in the lesson, and the worked example is a different problem.
- [ ] The problem and example are your own. Nothing is copied from a published test, textbook or website.
- [ ] `authors` and `license` are set. By opening the PR you license the lesson under that license.
- [ ] Title: `lesson: <topic>`.

## 7. What review rejects, and why

- Anything the validator rejects (CI runs it on every PR).
- The answer stated, shown or hinted to the point of giving it away: a student must still do their own problem (never verbatim).
- Questions copied from the SAT, ACT, AP or any published test or book: we cannot license them, and they would leak real test items.
- Wrong maths or science. A maintainer checks every worked step.
- Text instead of teaching: boards that are paragraphs, speech that reads a textbook aloud, no drawing.
- HTML, links, file paths or personal information anywhere (students see and hear every string).
- Changes to files other than your lesson.

## License

Lessons are CC-BY-4.0 unless the file says CC-BY-SA-4.0 or CC0-1.0. The site credits the `authors` you list.
